reasons: internal/mcp/budget.go:109 — the new `\n#### ` branch in `cutAtBoundary` is unconditional, so it also fires on `#### ` lines that are *file content*, not code-search hits. Measured on a read-file answer whose markdown has `#### ` subsections mid-window and a `### ` heading late: at the default 24 KiB budget the delivered body drops from 21,775 bytes (main) to 16,325 bytes (HEAD) — 25% less content for the same budget, because the cut now prefers an earlier content `#### ` over the later `### ` boundary main used. Reproduced at a second scale too (budget 3,400: 2,725 → 2,154 bytes). This is a content-delivery regression in read-file/query-docs/export-context, tools this change was not meant to touch, and the new tests do not cover it. Fix: scope both new branches to an actual code-search answer — only count/cut at `#### ` inside the region after the `### Source Matches (` heading.

internal/mcp/budget.go:104-108 — the comment states the blast radius as "An answer with no `#### ` gets -1 here and falls straight through", which is only true for answers with no `#### ` anywhere. Answers whose *content* contains `#### ` are silently affected, so the comment's stated scope and the code's actual scope disagree (the implementer's own note flagged this for `sectionCount` but not for `cutAtBoundary`).
notes: The core fix is real and the tests are real. I reverted internal/mcp/budget.go to main and re-ran the new tests: all four assertions in result_count_test.go fail pre-fix with exactly the output recorded in the ledger's `실패 재현:` line (result_count=3 want 2; notice says 2 exist but 50 found; last hit lost its `Source:` citation), and the three control-group cases pass pre-fix. The tests exercise the real Server.ServeHTTP round trip and count from the response rather than hardcoding — no always-true assertions.

Residual, NOT a regression, so not a reject reason: `clampResponse` compares `sectionCount(body)` (now `#### ` units) against `sectionCount(kept)` (falls back to `### ` units when the cut lands before the first hit), so a code-search answer with a long Repository Matches prelude reports "1 of 50 result sections are included" with zero hits in the body. I probed this on main too — it says "1 of 2" with zero hits in the identical case — so both are wrong and HEAD is not worse. Worth a follow-up idea: `shown` and `total` must be counted in the same unit.

Also not a regression: a single hit larger than ~40% of the room still cuts mid-hit (`enough()` floor), leaving a `#### ` heading with no `Source:` citation — measured identically on main and HEAD at budget 2000. The ledger's claim that the "last entry is whole" violation is fixed holds for the common case only.

Security (reviewer-class): no finding. The change only removes text from an already-ACL-filtered formatted answer; it cannot widen what a caller sees, touches no auth/session/ACL path, no secrets, no crypto, no untrusted input reaching a query (the SQL in the new test is parameterized), and no new dependency. `mcp_calls.result_count` is display/CSV/AVG only (internal/app/mcpadmin.go:223,440,479) with no control-flow consumer, so its value changing from 3 to N is the intended correction and exposes nothing new. Not blocking.

Legal/privacy (reviewer-class): no finding. No new personal data is collected, stored, or transmitted — `result_count` is a non-personal integer on an audit row that already existed; retention, access control and purpose are unchanged, no vendor or cross-border transfer, no license or copied code, no external-facing commitment. Not blocking.
